Making reports and preparing classes

Source: vignettes/reports.Rmd
reports.Rmd

render_report() produces a handout-style HTML report for any gene or region, with all the analyses from the other vignettes in one document. Reports can be printed, emailed or uploaded to a virtual learning environment as a single file. They are intended both as teaching material (results for students to interpret) and as a quick way for staff to explore a region.

Making a report 

library(snpscaper)

render_report("LCT")

This fetches the region, runs every analysis and saves snpscaper_LCT_staff.html in the current folder. It usually takes well under a minute.

The report contains:

  1. The region: its coordinates, and a short description for genes in teaching_genes.
  2. The data: the number of people per population, and the number of SNPs left after each filtering step.
  3. PCA: the first principal components, coloured by super-population and by population, and the share of variation each component captures.
  4. Admixture analysis: cross-entropy for each K, and ancestry proportions grouped by super-population and by population.
  5. Fst: a heatmap for pairs of populations, and a table for pairs of super-populations.
  6. Heterozygosity: a plot and a table for each population.
  7. Allele frequencies of key SNPs: a bar chart and a world map for each key SNP.
  8. Linkage disequilibrium: a heatmap for each super-population.
  9. Methods: data source, filters, settings, random seed, package version and references, so that results can be reproduced and cited.
  10. Notes for staff (staff version only): the expected pattern and its explanation.

Figures and tables are numbered, so students can refer to them (e.g. “Figure 6”) in their answers.

Staff and student versions

The staff version is the default. It adds notes on the expected patterns for genes in teaching_genes. The student version leaves these out:

render_report("LCT", version = "student")

Choosing what goes in 

render_report(
  "SLC24A5",
  pop = c("YRI", "LWK", "GBR", "FIN", "CHB", "JPT", "GIH", "PEL"),
  focal_snps = "rs1426654",
  k = 2:4,
  title = "Skin pigmentation: SLC24A5",
  output_dir = "handouts"
)
  • pop or super_pop choose the populations. Fewer populations make the plots easier to read.
  • focal_snps chooses the SNPs for the allele frequency section, as rs numbers or SNP IDs. By default the report uses the key SNPs in teaching_snps, or, for any other region, the SNP whose frequency differs most between super-populations.
  • k and reps control the admixture analysis, which is the slowest part.
  • min_maf sets the minor allele frequency filter.
  • seed makes the admixture results reproducible: the same settings always give the same report.

Several reports at once

Give several genes or regions to make one report for each:

render_report(
  c("LCT", "SLC24A5", "EDAR", "ALDH2", "ACKR1", "HBB"),
  version = "student",
  output_dir = "handouts"
)

Combining regions in one report

To analyse several regions together, fetch them first and pass the result:

pigmentation <- fetch_region(c("SLC24A5", "MC1R"))
render_report(pigmentation, title = "Pigmentation genes")

Preparing for a class

Fetching data in advance

Every region is downloaded once and then kept in a cache folder, so students working on the same regions do not all download them during the class. By default, each user has their own cache. To share one, set the cache folder before fetching, for example to a shared network drive:

options(snpscaper.cache_dir = "S:/teaching/snpscaper_cache")

for (gene in teaching_genes$gene) {
  fetch_region(gene)
}

Students then set the same option (for example at the top of a script you provide), and every fetch_region() call for those regions is instant and works offline.

Requirements

Reports need Quarto, which is installed with recent versions of RStudio, and the FactoMineR and factoextra packages. Fetching data needs internet access to ftp.1000genomes.ebi.ac.uk and, for genes not in teaching_genes, rest.ensembl.org.
